The relative speed between the ejecta and the Galaxy is \( v = 60\,000 \text{ km/s} \). The speed of light is \( c = 300\,000 \text{ km/s} \), so \( v/c = 0.2 \). The Lorentz factor is \( \gamma = 1/\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} = 1/\sqrt{1 - 0.04} = 1/\sqrt{0.96} \approx 1.0206 \).

The time interval in the ejecta frame is the proper time \( \Delta \tau = 50 \text{ s} \). In the Galaxy frame, the time elapsed is dilated: \( \Delta t = \gamma \Delta \tau \). The distance traveled by the ejecta in the Galaxy frame is \( d = v \Delta t = v \gamma \Delta \tau \).

Substituting the values:
\( d = 60\,000 \text{ km/s} \times 1.0206 \times 50 \text{ s} \approx 3\,061\,800 \text{ km} \).

This rounds to \( 3\,060\,000 \text{ km} \), which corresponds to option (D).

Answer: D
